<div class="pull-quote">Build ground truth once. Reuse it to evaluate every agentic workflow.</div>

## What success looks like

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.card}
<div class="card-title">Minimum viable benchmarks</div>

- Runnable transformation specification
- Representative source data
- Independently checked golden output
- Clear review history
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.card}
<div class="card-title">Human baseline</div>

- Experts review the same tasks
- Decisions are recorded, not implied
- Agent results are compared with an agreed reference
- Evaluation begins only after finalization
:::
:::
:::

::: callout-note
## Out of scope for now

Synthetic-data generation (supported by Keiji.ai members) and benchmark evaluation / leaderboard are later phases. The current priority is a trustworthy benchmark.
:::

# Community {background-color="#385898"}

## The human baseline is the work

<div class="flow">
<div class="flow-step">Create</div>
<div class="flow-step">Review</div>
<div class="flow-step">Discuss</div>
<div class="flow-step">Finalize</div>
<div class="flow-step">Evaluate</div>
</div>

- **Review a benchmark** — inspect the specification and golden output
- **Add comments** — challenge assumptions, clarity, and conformance
- **File issues** — record anything ambiguous or incorrect
- **Open pull requests** — contribute fixes and new benchmarks

## Anatomy of a benchmark

Every benchmark is a self-contained unit, ready for review:

```text
benchmarks/sdtm-dm-basic/
├── spec.yaml      # the specification under review
├── input/         # source data — ODM extracts, CSVs
├── expected/      # golden output: the human-verified truth
├── run.py, run.R  # one-command reproduction
└── README.md      # intent, mapping notes, lifecycle badge
```

To review: read the spec, check the golden output, leave a comment.
Your review moves a benchmark from `draft` to `reviewed`.

# Framework {background-color="#385898" data-state="no-corner-logo"}

![](../../assets/logo.jpeg){.hero-logo}

## yamaa in one slide

<div class="flow">
<div class="flow-step">Source data<br><span class="small">ODM, SDTM, files</span></div>
<div class="flow-step">yamaa spec<br><span class="small">explicit intent</span></div>
<div class="flow-step">Plan<br><span class="small">validate first</span></div>
<div class="flow-step">Engine<br><span class="small">Python or R</span></div>
<div class="flow-step">Outputs<br><span class="small">SDTM, ADaM, metadata</span></div>
</div>

A yamaa specification describes a deterministic transformation from clinical source data to standards-aligned datasets.

<span class="pill">one specification</span>
<span class="pill">one execution</span>
<span class="pill">reviewable lineage</span>
<span class="pill">runnable benchmark</span>

## The one principle

<div class="kicker">Determinism is a design constraint</div>

> A yamaa specification has exactly one execution. Where it would have two, yamaa fails instead of choosing.

Ambiguity is surfaced during planning — before it becomes a silent difference in the output.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**For people:** the specification is reviewable.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**For agents:** the expected behavior is testable.
:::
:::

## Four components

| Component | Purpose | Links |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema | Declares the vocabulary of the specification. | [Repository](https://github.com/elong0527/yamaa/tree/main/yaml) / [Introduction](https://elong0527.github.io/yamaa/articles/schema-intro/) |
| Rules | Defines the meaning of each specification. | [Repository](https://github.com/elong0527/yamaa/tree/main/yaml/rules) / [Rules](https://elong0527.github.io/yamaa/articles/rules/) |
| Engine | Runs specifications in Python and R according to the rules. | [Python](https://github.com/elong0527/yamaa/tree/main/python) / [R](https://github.com/elong0527/yamaa/tree/main/R/cdiscbuilder) |
| Benchmark | Provides runnable specification examples. | [Repository](https://github.com/elong0527/yamaa/tree/main/benchmark) / [Dashboards](https://elong0527.github.io/yamaa/benchmark/) |

### Deterministic by construction

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="47%"}
**Same inputs**

- Source data
- Specification
- Declared resources
:::
::: {.column width="6%"}
<div style="font-size:2rem; padding-top:3rem; text-align:center;">→</div>
:::
::: {.column width="47%"}
**Same result**

- Dataset values
- Validation outcome
- Execution lineage
:::
:::

<div class="pull-quote">Python and R should implement the same contract — not competing interpretations.</div>
